grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain cupboard staple such as curry powder, tinned chickpeas, tinned tomatoes and stock.

supermarket.reason: Jerusalem artichokes are stocked only patchily and at a premium in mainstream supermarkets like Tesco, so many readers could not buy the 400g the curry depends on.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, board and one large lidded pan, with simple softening and simmering.

works.reason: The quantities suit four, 2 tbsp curry powder with salt and lemon gives enough flavour, 500ml stock with a tin of tomatoes is a sensible liquid level, and 25 minutes will soften chunked carrots and artichokes.

honest_times.reason: 20 minutes is believable for chopping onions and carrots, scrubbing artichokes and shredding kale, and the steps add up to about 35 to 38 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming root-vegetable curry suits early February, and 500g of carrots leads the title and the pot.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Plenty of vegetables, two tins of chickpeas and yoghurt make a filling, wholesome family dinner.
